experiment: M1C — correction-kernel ablation (A vs B): single-mechanism test of the redistribution kernel
research_question: Does churn persist when the M1 selection rule is held fixed but the fixed biased redistribution law is replaced by a target-aware corrective kernel?
working_hypothesis_under_test: M1 late-stage persistent churn arises because the controller can locate where mass must be removed but the removed mass re-enters only through a fixed, exogenous, biased redistribution law q that cannot target the current deficit.

variants.A: canonical M1A/M1B baseline, untouched: removed mass resprayed with fixed q_near (redistribution='throw')
variants.B: selection identical (same cumulative-excess argmax, same alpha removal, same stopping rules); removed mass redistributed by target-aware deficit filling: deficit_i = max(1/K - p_minus_i, 0), add_i = M_removed * deficit_i / sum(deficit) (redistribution='deficit_fill')

single_change_declaration: Variant B differs from Variant A ONLY in the redistribution kernel. cumulative-excess definition, sweep-boundary rule, alpha, initial condition, target, stopping rules, metrics, K values and horizon are shared and unchanged.
invariants: mass conservation: sum(p_next) == sum(p_current) within float tolerance
non-negativity: no bin mass below zero
same selection: A and B use the identical canonical decision rule on the same current state
no local overfill: the corrective step never pushes a deficit bin above the uniform target (add_i <= deficit_i, guaranteed by total_deficit >= removed mass)
degenerate fallback: total deficit == 0 or removed > total deficit must raise, never silently fall back to q
throw_distribution: q_near(x) = 2(1-x); used by Variant A and by the shared initial condition
redistribution_B_target: u_i = 1/K (the uniform target already encoded by the selection rule and the U metric)
late_stage_definition: active rounds with D_max < 0.005 (M1B.2 convention), plus last-25%-of-active-rounds window; reported for both variants
no_post_hoc_tuning: single frozen mechanism per variant; results accepted as-is (falsification-oriented; no parameter, kernel or stopping adjustment after seeing trajectories)
mc_path_scope: Variant B is implemented for the deterministic expected-mass path only; all Stage-1 churn evidence (M1A.1/M1B/M1B.2) lives on that path. The MC particle path is out of scope for this ablation.
baseline_policy: if any Variant A reproduction check fails, M1C interpretation stops before any A-vs-B comparison (baseline divergence must be resolved first)
